sampling_model.design: I.i.d. superpopulation sampling from a fixed finite-stratum law.
sampling_model.treatment: The latent dose \(A_i\) is observed only through \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\); the errors are independent, nonidentically distributed, potentially asymmetric, and may have characteristic-function zero sets.
sampling_model.overlap: The finite strata have masses at least \(p_{\min}\), and \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) on \(I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly. An outward finite certificate uses \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) for discrepancy constraints and \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\) for ADRF endpoint evaluation, discards boxes with empty decoded law sets, and bounds width through the enlarged-profile inverse modulus.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The compact-support blind-replicate density estimator attains squared \(L^2\) risk of order \((\log\log n/\log n)^{2\beta}\), with a matching density lower bound.
The known-error continuous-treatment estimator admits pointwise asymptotic inference for the ADRF.

Theorems S11 and S12 give a uniform-in-treatment asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference for the ADRF when the continuous treatment is observed without measurement error.
A latent-variable variational framework estimates a continuous-treatment ADRF under measurement error with neural density models.
Inverting finite complex Kotlarski moment tests gives a uniformly size-controlled latent-density confidence band without imposing completeness.
A multiplier-bootstrap density band is uniformly valid when the unknown error law is learned from auxiliary data or symmetric repeated measurements.
Wavelet deconvolution estimators attain minimax sup-norm density rates under a known convolution operator.
Testing affinity yields lower bounds on confidence-band width over nonparametric function classes.
Under weak unconfoundedness and positivity, the error-free ADRF is identified by the continuous-treatment g-formula.

body.tldr: The observed law contains an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control of both channels on a moment-derived protected frequency square, followed by quantitative analytic continuation and Sobolev recovery, yields an honest simultaneous ADRF band with minimax expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\) for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\). A terminating outward-rounded profile uses a constraint tolerance \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) and a separate endpoint tolerance \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\): it outer-covers the exact profile, retains only nonempty decoded boxes, and confines every decoded law to a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile. The band width is obtained directly from the protected inverse modulus, without claiming numerical proximity to exact-profile extrema. A fixed-density Bernoulli marked experiment built from a weighted Jacobi packet and fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors supplies the matching lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Colangelo and Lee give uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is measured without error, and known-error measurement-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference. Blind repeated-measurement methods identify and estimate an unmarked density, and robust Kotlarski methods invert finite complex moments for density bands. None gives an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, or a fixed-nuisance marked converse when two replicate errors are unknown, asymmetric, nonidentical, and allowed to have spectral zeros; nor do they provide a finite law-valued outer certificate with distinct statistical-feasibility and endpoint tolerances.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both the density transform and the signed marked transform entire. A common second-moment radius supplies a uniform nonvanishing neighborhood by \(|\varphi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|\sqrt{M_e}\), so the protected square follows from a law-level moment condition. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient, and certificate maximality is secured by a discrepancy sandwich rather than by proximity to an exact optimizer.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the paired protected inverse at the sharp sup-norm exponent, embeds it in a continuously constrained confidence profile, and certifies a finite decoded outer profile using \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) for constraints and \(\zeta_n\) for endpoint arithmetic. Every retained endpoint box has a decoded feasible law, all decoded laws lie in a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile, and the inverse modulus therefore bounds the full certified endpoint diameter. A weighted Jacobi Bernoulli marked packet with fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors matches the upper width while leaving the complete unmarked replicate law fixed.

body.related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12 on pages 63--65 of the public manuscript, are the closest published uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator: they derive a uniform asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference over a compact treatment set when treatment is measured without error. Thus whole-curve ADRF inference itself is not the new obstacle; the obstacle is simultaneous inference after blind deconvolution with two unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric replicate errors. Huang and Zhang (2023) motivate the continuous-treatment measurement-error problem and derive pointwise ADRF inference when the error transform is known; their operator is not blind and their result is not simultaneous. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model, without a blind-replicate identification or honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy (2025) provide the closest method exemplar: their continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast achieves a nearly parametric local transform error and analytic continuation yields an unmarked density rate. The present construction adds a signed marked channel, a quotient, supremum loss, honest coverage, and a fixed-nuisance converse; its lower packet is a weighted Jacobi reproducing-kernel construction paired with new fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors, rather than a transplant of the comparator's density-packet construction. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) show how test inversion avoids fragile closed-form Kotlarski division, but their finite moments target an unmarked density and do not certify a continuum profile or sharp width. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) supply Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information. Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic functions as continuous probability coordinates. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform the sup-norm packing and band-width reduction. The Colangelo--Lee comparison is informed-by rather than a claimed tightening; the only equivalence claim is the explicit error-free reduction in Theorem 9.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite certificate must keep two numerical scales separate. Constraint boxes are refined to \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\), while ADRF evaluations are refined to \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\); outward feasibility alone does not place a numerical endpoint within \(O(\zeta_n)\) of an exact-profile extremum. Width instead follows by putting all nonempty decoded boxes inside a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile and applying the proved protected inverse modulus to decoded witnesses. For \(1/2<\beta\le3/2\), endpoint covering entropy enlarges the worst-case finite-certificate count; only \(\beta>3/2\) yields the simpler \(K_n^2\) coordinate regime. On the converse side, the weighted Jacobi packet must preserve the Bernoulli range, strict Sobolev slack, fixed nuisance laws, and product-law total variation.
body.honest_scope: The frontier holds for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\), with the support interval, Sobolev radii, overlap constants, outcome bound, and common error second-moment radius fixed. Error distributions remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zero sets away from the moment-derived protected neighborhood. The finite certificate terminates throughout this range, although its simpler \(K_n^2\) complexity regime requires \(\beta>3/2\). Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. When \(U_1=U_2=0\), Theorem 9 recovers the standard error-free g-formula.
